messages.content: 你能使用 get_stock_prices 函數來檢索蘋果、微軟、亞馬遜和特斯拉分別在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內的股價嗎？。

function.name: get_stock_prices
function.description: Retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

companies.description: List of companies to retrieve stock prices for.

duration.description: Time duration to retrieve stock prices for. E.g., '1 week', '2 weeks', '1 month', etc.

The user wants to use the get_stock_prices function to retrieve stock prices for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Tesla for durations 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, 1 month. The function signature expects companies: string[], duration: string. But we need to provide separate calls? The user says "retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration". They want to retrieve for each company separately? Or maybe they want to retrieve all four companies for each duration? The function only accepts one duration per call. So we might need to make multiple calls: one for each duration. But the user specifically says "for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Tesla respectively in 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks and 1 month time ranges." That could mean: Apple for 1 week, Microsoft for 2 weeks, Amazon for 3 weeks, Tesla for 1 month. So each company gets a different duration. So we can call get_stock_prices with companies ["Apple"] and duration "1 week", then ["Microsoft"], "2 weeks", etc.

Thus we need to produce function calls. According to guidelines, we should output JSON with name and arguments. We can do multiple calls? The guidelines say we can only output one function call at a time. But we can chain calls. So we need to output the first function call. Then after receiving result, we can call next. But we don't have results yet. So we need to ask for the first call. But the user asked to retrieve all. We can interpret as we need to retrieve all four. We can do multiple calls sequentially. So we output the first call: get_stock_prices({"companies": ["Apple"], "duration": "1 week"}). Then after we get result, we can call next. But we can't output multiple calls at once. So we need to ask for the first call. But the user didn't specify which order. We can choose Apple first. So we output the function call for Apple. Then we will get result. Then we can call next. But the user might expect us to retrieve all at once. But the function only supports one duration. So we need to clarify. But we can proceed with sequential calls. So we output the first call.
